Encoded as: 0=operating, 1=no-power, 2=service, 3=stopped, 4=not-defined, 5=definition-error, 6=suspended, 7=check-stopped, 8=wrap-block, 9=permanent-error, 10=loss-of-signal, 11=loss-of-synchronization, 12=not-operational-link, 99=unknown.

**[1] `mainframe.adapter.name`:** The channel subsystem (CSS) index and channel path identifier (CHPID) are concatenated with a dot separator, e.g., "0.2D" for CSS 0, CHPID 2D. Reported by the HMC Web Services API adapter object field `adapter-id`.

## `mainframe.adapter.utilization`

| Name | Instrument Type | Unit (UCUM) | Description | Stability | Entity Associations |
| -------- | --------------- | ----------- | -------------- | --------- | ------ |
| `mainframe.adapter.utilization` | Gauge | `1` | The fraction of time the mainframe I/O adapter was busy processing I/O or requests, as a ratio from 0 (idle) to 1 (fully utilised). [3] | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `mainframe.adapter` |

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**[3]:** Reported by the IBM Z HMC Web Services API. In DPM mode, source is the `adapter-usage` metric group field `adapter-usage`. In classic mode, sources are `crypto-usage` field `adapter-usage` (HMC >= 2.12.0), `flash-memory-usage` field `adapter-usage` (HMC >= 2.12.0). SC27-2646-01 v2.17.0 declares no `roce-usage` metric group; RoCE adapter utilization is reported through the DPM `adapter-usage` group. Note that the classic-mode `crypto-usage` and `flash-memory-usage` groups have Applicable Managed Object Class `cpc`, not `adapter`: one entry is produced per adapter, and the adapter identity must be reconstructed from the in-group `channel-id` (and `crypto-id` for cryptos) rather than taken from the object the metric group is attached to. The HMC reports an integer percentage (0-100), which is divided by 100 to yield the 0-1 ratio this metric declares. Use `mainframe.adapter.type` to distinguish adapter categories. Analogous to NIC, HBA, or RDMA NIC utilization.

**Attributes:**

| Key | Stability | [Requirement Level](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/general/attribute-requirement-level/) | Value Type | Description | Example Values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mainframe.adapter.name` | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Required` | string | The name of the I/O adapter in the form CSS.Chpid. [4] | `0.00`; `0.2D`; `1.E3` |
| `mainframe.adapter.type` | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Required` | string | The type of the mainframe I/O adapter card. [5] | `crypto`; `flash`; `roce` |

**[4] `mainframe.adapter.name`:** The channel subsystem (CSS) index and channel path identifier (CHPID) are concatenated with a dot separator, e.g., "0.2D" for CSS 0, CHPID 2D. Reported by the HMC Web Services API adapter object field `adapter-id`.

**[5] `mainframe.adapter.type`:** Reported by the HMC Web Services API adapter object field `type`. Used to distinguish network, storage, cryptographic, and accelerator adapters when aggregating per-type utilization metrics.

---

`mainframe.adapter.type` has the following list of well-known values. If one of them applies, then the respective value MUST be used; otherwise, a custom value MAY be used.

| Value | Description | Stability |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `accelerator` | An accelerator adapter, providing hardware acceleration for specific workloads such as compression or AI inference. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `crypto` | A cryptographic (crypto) adapter, providing hardware-accelerated encryption and key management. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `flash` | A Flash Express adapter, providing solid-state storage for IBM Virtual Flash Memory (VFM). | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `network` | A network adapter providing connectivity to external networks. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `roce` | A RDMA over Converged Ethernet (RoCE) adapter, providing low-latency RDMA networking over Ethernet. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `storage` | A storage adapter providing connectivity to external storage systems such as SAN or NVMe-oF. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |

## `mainframe.channel.utilization`

| Name | Instrument Type | Unit (UCUM) | Description | Stability | Entity Associations |
| -------- | --------------- | ----------- | -------------- | --------- | ------ |
| `mainframe.channel.utilization` | Gauge | `1` | The fraction of time the I/O channel path was busy processing I/O, as a ratio from 0 (idle) to 1 (fully utilised). [4] | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `mainframe.channel` |

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**[4]:** Reported by the IBM Z HMC Web Services API channel-usage metric group field `channel-usage` (classic mode). The HMC reports an integer percentage (0-100), which is divided by 100 to yield the 0-1 ratio this metric declares. A channel path identifier (CHPID) is the unique identifier for a hardware I/O channel. Use the `mainframe.channel.name` attribute in CSS.CHPID format to identify the specific channel path. In distributed systems terms, this is analogous to the link utilization of a network interface or storage HBA port.

**Attributes:**

| Key | Stability | [Requirement Level](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/general/attribute-requirement-level/) | Value Type | Description | Example Values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mainframe.channel.name` | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Required` | string | The name of the I/O channel in the form CSS.Chpid. [6] | `0.00`; `0.2D`; `1.E3` |
| `mainframe.channel.mode` | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | The operating mode of the I/O channel — either dedicated to a single partition or shared across partitions. | `dedicated`; `shared` |

**[6] `mainframe.channel.name`:** The channel subsystem (CSS) index and channel path identifier (CHPID) are concatenated with a dot separator, e.g., "0.2D" for CSS 0, CHPID 2D. Reported by the HMC Web Services API channel-path object.

---

`mainframe.channel.mode` has the following list of well-known values. If one of them applies, then the respective value MUST be used; otherwise, a custom value MAY be used.

| Value | Description | Stability |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dedicated` | The I/O channel is dedicated to a specific partition and cannot be shared with other partitions. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `shared` | The I/O channel can be shared among multiple partitions and is not dedicated to a specific partition. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |

## `mainframe.cpu.smt_mode.utilization`

| Name | Instrument Type | Unit (UCUM) | Description | Stability | Entity Associations |
| -------- | --------------- | ----------- | -------------- | --------- | ------ |
| `mainframe.cpu.smt_mode.utilization` | Gauge | `1` | The fraction of time the processor was running in simultaneous multithreading (SMT) mode, as a ratio from 0 to 1. [5] | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `mainframe.cpu` |

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**[5]:** Reported by the IBM Z HMC Web Services API CPC metric group `zcpc-processor-usage` field `smt-usage` (all modes). A value of -1 indicates that the mainframe model does not support simultaneous multithreading (SMT). When SMT is active, a single physical processor executes two hardware threads concurrently (SMT-2), improving instruction throughput.

**[7] `mainframe.cpu.name`:** Reported by the HMC Web Services API processor object. In distributed systems terms, a mainframe processor is analogous to a physical CPU core.

## `mainframe.host.adapter.utilization`

| Name | Instrument Type | Unit (UCUM) | Description | Stability | Entity Associations |
| -------- | --------------- | ----------- | -------------- | --------- | ------ |
| `mainframe.host.adapter.utilization` | Gauge | `1` | The fraction of time adapters of the specified type on the Central Processing Complex (CPC) were busy processing I/O, as a ratio from 0 (idle) to 1 (fully utilised). [9] | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `virtualization.platform` |

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**[9]:** Reported by the IBM Z HMC Web Services API CPC metric group `dpm-system-usage-overview` (DPM mode only). Use the `mainframe.adapter.type` attribute to select the adapter category: network (`network-usage`), storage (`storage-usage`), accelerator (`accelerator-usage`), or crypto (`crypto-usage`). The HMC reports an integer percentage (0-100), which is divided by 100 to yield the 0-1 ratio this metric declares. A value of -1 indicates no adapters of the specified type are present. Collected by the HMC at 15-second intervals. In distributed systems terms, this is analogous to aggregate NIC, HBA, or accelerator utilization on a server.

**Attributes:**

## `mainframe.host.cpu.utilization`

| Name | Instrument Type | Unit (UCUM) | Description | Stability | Entity Associations |
| -------- | --------------- | ----------- | -------------- | --------- | ------ |
| `mainframe.host.cpu.utilization` | Gauge | `1` | The fraction of time processors of the specified type in the Central Processing Complex (CPC) were busy, as a ratio from 0 (idle) to 1 (fully utilised). [16] | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `virtualization.platform` |

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**[16]:** Reported by the IBM Z HMC Web Services API CPC metric group `cpc-usage-overview` (classic mode). The group reports one field per processor type and sharing mode: `<type>-all-processor-usage`, `<type>-shared-processor-usage` and `<type>-dedicated-processor-usage` for each of cp, ifl, icf and iip. Select the field using the `mainframe.cpu.type` attribute, and `mainframe.cpu.sharing.mode` where set (the `-all-` field is the aggregate across both sharing modes). The HMC reports an integer percentage (0-100), which is divided by 100 to yield the 0-1 ratio this metric declares. A value of -1 indicates no processors of the specified type are installed. In distributed systems terms, this is analogous to `system.cpu.utilization` aggregated across all cores of a given type.

## `mainframe.partition.cpu.utilization`

| Name | Instrument Type | Unit (UCUM) | Description | Stability | Entity Associations |
| -------- | --------------- | ----------- | -------------- | --------- | ------ |
| `mainframe.partition.cpu.utilization` | Gauge | `1` | The fraction of time processors of the specified type allocated to the logical partition (LPAR) were busy, as a ratio from 0 (idle) to 1 (fully utilised). [32] | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `virtualization.partition` |

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**[32]:** Reported by the IBM Z HMC Web Services API logical-partition-usage metric group (classic mode) fields `cp-processor-usage`, `ifl-processor-usage`, `icf-processor-usage` and `iip-processor-usage` — select with the `mainframe.cpu.type` attribute. In DPM mode the partition-usage metric group (HMC >= 2.13.1) reports only an aggregate `processor-usage` field with no per-type breakdown, so `mainframe.cpu.type` is not set there. The HMC reports an integer percentage (0-100), which is divided by 100 to yield the 0-1 ratio this metric declares. In distributed systems terms, this is analogous to the per-type CPU utilization of a virtual machine.

**[23] `mainframe.storage.group.volume.name`:** Reported by the HMC Web Services API storage-volume resource object field `name` (DPM mode only, HMC ≥ 2.14.1). A storage volume is a single logical unit of block storage (LUN / ECKD DASD cylinder set / NVMe namespace) within a storage group.

**[24] `host.name`:** The name of the Central Processing Complex (CPC) that owns the storage group containing this volume.

**[25] `mainframe.storage.fulfillment.state`:** Reported by the HMC Web Services API storage-group or storage-volume object field `fulfillment-state` (DPM mode only, HMC ≥ 2.14.1). In distributed systems terms, this is analogous to the binding phase of a Kubernetes Persistent Volume Claim.

---

`mainframe.storage.fulfillment.state` has the following list of well-known values. If one of them applies, then the respective value MUST be used; otherwise, a custom value MAY be used.

| Value | Description | Stability |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `checking-migration` | The storage resource is being checked for migration eligibility. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `complete` | The storage resource is fully configured and available. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `configuration-error` | The storage volume has a configuration error. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `deleting` | The storage volume is being deleted. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `incomplete` | The storage resource is incompletely configured and not fully available. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `overprovisioned` | The storage volume is overprovisioned. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `pending` | The storage resource is pending configuration by the storage administrator. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `pending-with-mismatches` | The storage resource is pending but has configuration mismatches that must be resolved. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
